newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- ends unchanged to up 1/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- ends unchanged to up 1/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices finished Tuesday's session unchanged to up about 1/8 point.
Market participants said the light new issue calendar and a firmer Treasury market helped give munis a better tone.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was higher, gaining 4/32 at 98-7/32 to yield 6.51 percent. There was little noticeable bond market reaction at mid-afternoon when the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, as expected, left interest rates unchanged.

In debt futures, the September municipal contract ended 7/32 higher at 120-12/32. The September T-bond contract gained 3/32 to 114-6/32, widening the MOB spread to 198 ticks from 194 at the close on Monday.

John Nuveen & Co repriced Tuesday's largest negotiated offering, a $79.5 million Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs revenue bond deal. Nuveen lowered the yield in 2013 five basis points, to 5.25 percent.
On the competitive side, 19 sales totaling $239 million were scheduled. JP Morgan Securities won the day's largest competitive deal, a $62 million Fort Bend Independent School District, Texas, issue.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday were expected to total $1.2 billion in 33 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $835 million in 21 sales, with a $200 million St. Louis, Mo., offering through Bear, Stearns and Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $345 million were scheduled. A $250 million Florida Board of Education offering at 1100 EDT was the largest. --Steven Dickson, 212-859-1652
